examples.ko: 내일 친구 가게 개업식에 가기로 했어요.
examples.en: I'm going to my friend's shop opening ceremony tomorrow.

examples.ko: 개업식 날 손님들에게 떡을 나눠 줬어요.
examples.en: On opening day we handed out rice cakes to the guests.

examples.ko: 개업식이 끝나고 다 같이 점심을 먹었어요.
examples.en: After the opening ceremony, we all had lunch together.
It's a small restaurant, so we kept the opening ceremony simple.
At the opening, the owner gave a short greeting.

examples.ko: 개업식을 앞두고 가게 청소를 하느라 바빠요.
examples.en: I'm busy cleaning the shop ahead of the opening ceremony.

explain: '개업'은 가게나 병원 같은 일을 처음 시작하는 것이고, '개업식'은 그때 하는 행사예요. 반대말은 '폐업'이에요. 개업 선물로는 화분을 많이 주고, 개업 떡을 돌리기도 해요.
explain_en: '개업' is starting a business such as a shop or clinic, and '개업식' is the event held then. The opposite is '폐업' (closing down). Potted plants are a popular gift, and some owners hand out rice cakes.

en: to open; to start; to launch

examples.en: My uncle opens a restaurant next month.
The doctor opened a clinic in the neighborhood.
It has been a year since we opened.
That bakery became popular as soon as it opened.

examples.ko: 개업하기 전에 준비할 게 정말 많아요.
examples.en: There is a lot to prepare before opening a business.
I want to open a cafe someday.

explain: '개업하다'는 가게나 사무실을 처음 열고 영업을 시작하는 거예요. 매일 아침 문을 여는 건 '문을 열다'라고 해요. 영업을 완전히 그만두는 건 '폐업하다'예요.
explain_en: 개업하다 is opening a shop or office and starting business for the first time. Opening the door each morning is '문을 열다'. Closing a business for good is 폐업하다.

dis.h: start running a business or practice

p.n: 개점 focuses on the store opening, not on starting to run a business.

examples.en: I heard there's a gas meter reading this morning.

examples.ko: 수도 검침을 하러 직원이 집에 왔어요.
examples.en: A staff member came to the house to read the water meter.

examples.ko: 검침 결과가 고지서에 잘못 나와서 전화했어요.
examples.en: The meter reading was wrong on the bill, so I called.
The meter reader knocked on the door, so I went out to see.

examples.ko: 검침은 몇 분이면 끝나니까 잠깐만 기다려 주세요.
examples.en: The meter reading only takes a few minutes, so please wait a moment.

examples.ko: 이번 달 검침에 오류가 있었는지 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Please check whether there was an error in this month's meter reading.

explain: 가스, 전기, 수도 계량기의 숫자를 읽는 일에 써요. 이 일을 하는 사람은 '검침원'이라고 하고, 요금 고지서와 함께 자주 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is used for reading the numbers on gas, electricity or water meters. The person who does it is called a '검침원', and the word often comes up together with utility bills.

en: to take over; to take charge of

examples.en: A big company takes over a small one.
My older brother took over the shop.
I will take delivery of my new car tomorrow.
The takeover price is so high that I am worried.

examples.ko: 업무를 인수하고 나서 매일 늦게까지 일했어요.
examples.en: After taking over the work, I worked late every day.

examples.ko: 물건을 인수한 뒤 문제가 있으면 말해 주세요.
examples.en: After you receive the item, please tell me if there is a problem.

explain: 회사나 가게를 사서 이어받거나, 물건과 업무를 넘겨받을 때 써요. 반대말은 넘겨주는 '인계하다'이고, 일을 넘기고 받는 과정을 '인수인계'라고 한 세트로 말해요. 신문에서는 회사 이야기에 가장 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Used for buying and taking over a company or shop, or for receiving goods and duties. The opposite is '인계하다' (hand over), and the whole handover process is called '인수인계'. In newspapers it most often appears in company news.

en: to promote; to publicize; to advertise

examples.en: The company promotes its new product.
I want to promote our club.
City hall publicized the festival yesterday.
I am looking for a way to promote the shop.
Many people promote things on the internet.
I told my friends about it, and customers increased.

explain: '광고하다'는 돈을 내고 알리는 느낌이 강하고, '홍보하다'는 널리 알려서 좋은 이미지를 만든다는 느낌이에요. 회사, 학교, 지역 행사 이야기에서 자주 써요. '홍보 담당', '홍보물'처럼 명사로도 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Compared with the word for paying for an ad, this one stresses spreading information to build a good image. It is common for companies, schools and local events, and the noun form appears in words for PR staff and PR materials.
